SELECTED_INDEX: 2
CONFIDENCE: 0.63
EXPLANATION: A very strong Raman line at 2233 cm⁻¹ identifies a C≡N stretch; candidate 2 (p-tolunitrile) contains a nitrile group.  
Additional key bands match an aromatic methyl-substituted benzene:  
• 1610 cm⁻¹ – aromatic C=C stretch of the ring.  
• 1382 cm⁻¹ – CH₃ symmetric bend of the para-methyl group.  
• 1180 / 1200 cm⁻¹ – ring + CH₃ in-plane deformations common to p-methylbenzenes.  
• 822  &  801 cm⁻¹ – out-of-plane C–H bends characteristic of para-substituted benzenes.  
• 3073  &  2930 cm⁻¹ – aromatic and aliphatic C–H stretches, respectively.  
Low-frequency ring deformations appear at 653  and  552 cm⁻¹.  
No strong carbonyl (≈1700 cm⁻¹), S=O or C–Cl bands are seen, ruling out candidates that contain those groups (1, 3, 4, 5). The required methyl band excludes nitrile candidates lacking CH₃ (9). Altogether, the observed spectrum best fits p-tolunitrile (candidate 2).
